# CYSTEMD v4 → v5 migration

Generated by `cystemd migrate`. Every file here is a starting point: review
it, keep it in version control, and follow the steps below. The general
guide is docs/MIGRATION.md in the CYSTEMD repository.

## Applications

`applications.yaml` holds one Application per `continuous_deployment` entry.
Each runs its unit on every node of its pool (`replicas: 0`, `nodeSelector`),
as v4 did on every host of the pool.

| Application | v4 service | Pool | Branch | Values | Secret | Sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `myproject_myapplication-myapplication` | myproject_myapplication | myapplication | master | products/myproject/environments/dev/myproject_myapplication/values.yaml | kubernetes/myproject/myapplication/myproject-myapplication-dev | automated, self-heal |
| `myproject_myapplication2` | myproject_myapplication2 | myapplication2 | releasedev | products/myproject/environments/dev/myproject_myapplication2/values.yaml | — | manual (v4 autosync off) |
| `payments-api` | Payments@API | myapplication2 | master | payments/values.yaml | — | automated, self-heal |
| `myproject_myapplication-poc` | myproject_myapplication | poc | master | products/myproject/environments/poc/myproject_myapplication/values.yaml | kubernetes/myproject/poc | automated, self-heal |

## Hosts

`hosts/<host>.hcl` is each host's Nomad client configuration: its node pools
as client meta (`cystemd_selector_<pool>`) and the systemd driver's
allowlists for exactly the units, packages and directories of its
applications.

| Host | Pools | Applications |
|---|---|---|
| HOST001 | myapplication, poc | myproject_myapplication-myapplication, myproject_myapplication-poc |
| host002 | myapplication, myapplication2 | myproject_myapplication-myapplication, myproject_myapplication2, payments-api |
| HOST009 | poc | myproject_myapplication-poc |

| File | Install |
|---|---|
| `applications.yaml` | `cystemd app create -f applications.yaml` |
| `control-plane.hcl` | merge into the control plane configuration on the server hosts |
| `hosts/HOST001.hcl` | `/etc/cystemd/agent.d/90-migrated.hcl` on that host |
| `hosts/HOST009.hcl` | `/etc/cystemd/agent.d/90-migrated.hcl` on that host |
| `hosts/host002.hcl` | `/etc/cystemd/agent.d/90-migrated.hcl` on that host |
| `vault-agent/templates/app.ctmpl` | `/etc/vault-agent/templates/` on those hosts |
| `vault-agent/templates/other.ctmpl` | `/etc/vault-agent/templates/` on those hosts |
| `vault-agent/vault-agent.hcl` | `/etc/vault-agent/vault-agent.hcl` on every host that used VAULT_TEMPLATES |
| `vault/apply.sh` | run once with a Vault admin token |
| `vault/policies/cystemd-app-myproject_myapplication-myapplication.hcl` | Vault policy (written by vault/apply.sh) |
| `vault/policies/cystemd-app-myproject_myapplication-poc.hcl` | Vault policy (written by vault/apply.sh) |
| `vault/roles/cystemd-app-myproject_myapplication-myapplication.json` | Vault JWT role (written by vault/apply.sh) |
| `vault/roles/cystemd-app-myproject_myapplication-poc.json` | Vault JWT role (written by vault/apply.sh) |

## Steps

1. Set up Consul, Vault and the Nomad ACLs (deploy/README.md, step 1).
2. Start the server agents with the control plane, merging `control-plane.hcl` into their control plane configuration.
3. Write the applications' Vault policies and roles: `VAULT_ADDR=… VAULT_TOKEN=… vault/apply.sh`.
4. On each host, stop the v4 daemon (`systemctl disable --now cystemd`), install the cystemd agent with `deploy/agent/client.hcl` and the host's `hosts/<host>.hcl`, and start it. The units keep running; nothing touches them until their application syncs.
5. Install the host Vault Agent: `vault-agent/vault-agent.hcl` and `vault-agent/templates/` (see Files).
6. Log in (`cystemd login <server>`) and create the applications: `cystemd app create -f applications.yaml`. Automated ones sync at once; to review them first, drop their `syncPolicy` from the file, check `cystemd app diff <name>`, sync with `cystemd app sync <name>`, then `cystemd app set <name> -sync-policy=automated -self-heal`.
7. The first sync restarts each unit once, so that it runs with the task's environment, secrets and limits (v4 restarted on every change too). Watch them in the UI.

## Not carried over

- `version: v4.9.1`: v4 updated its own package. Upgrade the cystemd agent like any Nomad agent (one host at a time).
- `listen_address`: the API and UI are served on the Nomad agent's HTTP address (`/api/`, `/ui/`).
- `vault.renewal_*`: Vault Agent and Nomad renew tokens and leases themselves.
- `VAULT_PATH`/`VAULT_ENV_FILE`: v4's own environment; the agent reads no .env. If other software reads that file, add a template to the host Vault Agent (`vaultagent.EnvTemplate` renders the same KEY="value" format).
- `replica` (v4 ignored it): an application runs on every node of its pool; set `replicas: N` to run N instances instead.
- Credentials (`VAULT_ROLE_ID`, `VAULT_SECRET_ID`, `VAULT_TOKEN`, `GIT_SSH_KEY_PRIVATE`, …) are never copied: install them where the files above reference them.

## Warnings

- no_values: no git_values; v5 renders a systemd source from a values file, so it is skipped
- continuous_deployment[5] has no service: skipped
- host HOST001: myproject_myapplication-myapplication and myproject_myapplication-poc both manage myproject_myapplication.service (v4 managed the first entry only); keep the host in one of their pools
- copy the Git SSH key /opt/cystemd/.ssh/id_ed25519 (GIT_SSH_KEY_PRIVATE) to the control plane hosts
- copy the v4 JWT public key /opt/cystemd/jwt.pub to the control plane hosts
- v4 skipped Vault TLS verification by default; the Vault Agent verifies it: set vault.ca_cert in vault-agent/vault-agent.hcl if Vault's certificate is not issued by a system CA
- template testdata/templates/app.tmpl: line 4: field "api-key" is read with index, which renders an empty value instead of failing when it is missing
- template testdata/templates/missing.tmpl: open testdata/templates/missing.tmpl: no such file or directory; convert it by hand into vault-agent/templates/missing.ctmpl (see MIGRATION.md)
- template other.tmpl: line 2 calls secret with a non-literal path: convert it by hand

Secrets are read as KV version 2 (v4 tried v2, then v1). Pass `-kv-version=1` if their mounts are KV v1.
